judge_output.rationale: No listed work compares SPHEREx 3.5-5 um excess between a large multi-survey dipper sample and Gaia-matched controls. Closely related checks exist with WISE-band data for individual dippers or small samples: Tzanidakis et al. (2025) report no IR excess among 81 ZTF main-sequence dipper candidates, Boyajian et al. (2016) find no significant IR excess for KIC 8462852, and Marshall et al. (2023) find a NEOWISE 3.4/4.6 um excess for ASASSN-21qj. Ansdell et al. (2016) tested a dip-depth versus W2-excess relation, but only in young disk-hosting dippers, which the card excludes.

closest_prior.relation: Examined archival IR data for 81 ZTF main-sequence dipper candidates and reported no IR excess or variability, using WISE-era photometry, without a matched-control population statistic or SPHEREx spectra.
Found a positive correlation between dip depth and WISE-2 excess in ten young K2 dippers in Upper Sco/Oph, a YSO population the card explicitly excludes.
Single-star case: NEOWISE 3.4/4.6 um excess in the Boyajian-like dipper ASASSN-21qj, attributed to dust; no control comparison.
SED fitting of KIC 8462852 showed no significant IR excess; this is one object, the F3V star used in the card's own mechanism estimate.

judge_output.what_would_make_it_open: An analysis would need to deliver a population-level median 3.5-5 um excess difference, measured with SPHEREx spectrophotometry, between about 500 Kepler/K2/TESS/ZTF field dippers and Gaia-matched controls, which no listed work provides.
